Standing Counsel
 Coram:
 Justice S.K. Sahoo
 Order
This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Learned counsel for the State submits that notice on the informant has been made sufficient on 25.05.2023.
None appears for the informant.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and leaned counsel for the State.

This is an appeal under section 14-A of S.C. & S.T. (PoA) Act, 1989 in connection with Special Case No.79 of 2022 arising out of Sahadevkhunta P.S. Case No.300 of 2022 pending in the Court of learned Special Court (SC & // 2 // ST), Balasore for offences punishable under sections 395/307/376-D/34 of the Indian Penal Code, under sections 25/27 of the Arms Act and under section 3(2)(v) of the S.C. & S.T. (PoA) Act.

The appellant moved an application for bail before the Court of learned Special Court (SC & ST),
Balasore, which was rejected on 22.03.2023.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that earlier the appellant approached this Court for bail in CRLA No.970 of 2022 which was rejected as per the order dated 21.02.2023, however, liberty was granted to the appellant to renew his prayer for bail after examination of the victim in the learned trial Court.

Learned counsel further submitted that in the meantime, the victim has been examined as P.W.1 and the victim and her husband were the indentifying witnesses but none of them identified the appellant in the test identification parade and one of the co-accused Bapun @ Bapun Sing @ Kanka Singh who was not identified in the T.I. parade has been released on bail by this Court in CRLA No.1047 of 2022 as per the order dated 25.01.2023.
Learned counsel files the copy of the bail order, which is taken on record.
Learned counsel further submitted that in view of the nature of evidence available on record, the bail application of the appellant may be favourably considered.
Learned counsel filed the // 3 // deposition copy of the informant so also the test identification parade report, which are also taken on record.

Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the victim-informant has named the appellant in the F.I.R. and 164 Cr.P.C. statement but she stated to have come to know about the name of the appellant during conversation of the accused persons.
Perused the statement of the victim (P.W.1) so also the 164 Cr.P.C. statement and test identification parade report.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, change in the circumstances after rejection of the earlier bail application, release of the co-accused on bail and progress of the trial so far, I am inclined to reconsider the prayer for bail and direct release him on bail.
Let the appellant be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/-
(rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin over the matter with such terms and conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper including the conditions that the appellant shall not indulge in any criminal activities,
shall appear before // 4 // the learned trial Court when the case would be posted for trial and shall not try to tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
The CRLA is accordingly disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of this order on proper application.

( S.K. Sahoo) Judge Sipun Designation: Junior Stenographer Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA Date: 22-Jun-2023 16:26:11 Sonu @ Debendra Singh vs State Of Odisha on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132734690/
